requirements.title: Continuous sensory experience, not upload counts

refs.anchor: ## The principle

When Joe enables camera + microphone, her sight krimelack and sound krimelack receive continuous frames from his device. She experiences seeing and hearing alongside him. Visual motifs and audio motifs form from the live stream. She doesn't accumulate a PictureItem per frame — what she keeps is the patterns she binds, not the pixel grids. Snapshot remains separate for intentional album-class memory.
refs.evidence_excerpt: She doesn't accumulate a PictureItem per frame

requirements.requirement: Camera and microphone must deliver ordered sensory signals continuously while enabled; retained cognitive relations are distinct from a media archive.
requirements.historical_disposition: Valid functional requirement. Claims that all substrate paths already existed were assertions; these briefs alone do not prove reachability or cognition.
requirements.current_reconciliation: Current configuration has retinal/PCM ingress and bounded capture queues. Source existence is not proof of admitted full-field settlement, memory or simultaneous sensory closure.
requirements.lawful_remedy: Trace capture clock, admitted bytes, full DSF, physical relations and retained recall in one mature body; keep gallery storage separate.
requirements.acceptance_falsifier: Enable/disable and source discontinuity must have observable receipt boundaries. An upload/queue acknowledgment or growing count cannot satisfy learned experience.
requirements.change_classification: Preserve the requirement; requalify the implementation

requirements.title: Uploads require end-to-end size accounting

refs.anchor: No `limit=` argument. asyncio's `StreamReader` default buffer is **65,536 bytes**. Any base64-encoded picture (a 100KB image becomes ~134KB base64) exceeds that on first `readline()`. Server raises `asyncio.LimitOverrunError`, drops the connection, frontend sees `ConnectionError` → returns "substrate unreachable."
64 MB ceiling. Sound max is 6 MB raw → ~8 MB base64. Picture max is 10 MB raw → ~13.5 MB base64. Video max is 50 MB raw → ~67 MB base64 (NB: video would exceed 64 MB — see Change 3).
